canonical_data: conversations, messages, stores (chat applications), vector-indexed knowledge, tool and policy records, and usage and audit logs in the operator's MySQL or SQLite database
current_repo_note: The default configuration still names its database casibase, and sign-in goes through a Casdoor SDK. The 54 bundled skills under skills/ carry no licence files of their own; the root Apache-2.0 file is the only licence in the tree.
strengths: One workspace fronts many providers and per-conversation model choice, with per-store knowledge bases, embeddings and file ingestion, plus MCP, browser, shell and Office tools exposed to the model
Ships as a single binary with a native Windows build and falls back to SQLite when MySQL is absent, with a read-only demo and a resettable playground to try first
Operators get usage and cost analytics, request logs, audit records and owner-scoped multi-tenancy, and the README lists OIDC, OAuth2, LDAP and SAML sign-in through its auth layer
weaknesses: A tool-permission engine and a ToolPolicy table with allow, ask and deny rules exist, but a search of the Go sources finds no call that checks them when a tool runs, so the rules appear to be stored without being enforced
The tool-calling loop continues while the model keeps requesting tools, with no round limit in the loop code
A fast release train (v2.95.1 days after v2.94.x) and a replaced front end, with the previous Ant Design interface kept only for reference, mean the product surface is still moving
why_it_matters: A broadly featured open alternative to hosted multi-model chat products that also bundles agent tools and administration, useful as a comparison point for LibreChat-style deployments.
